newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Payout to TVK delayed on legal issues.
newsitem.headline: Payout to TVK delayed on legal issues.

text.p: A payout to chemicals maker TVK by Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt, already taken for granted by the stock market, will be delayed by legal uncertainties, APV said on Wednesday.

Market talk about an imminent payout to the company under Hungary's privatisation regulations boosted the price of TVK shares to record levels on Wednesday on the Budapest Stock Exchange and on London's SEAQ.
APV CEO Pal Szabo denied the news, saying that APV will pay to TVK what is due under the law but he "had some question marks" concerning the draft of APV's decision on the payout.
"I gave the whole thing, as it was, back (to APV experts) to check the legality," he told a news conference. "This is about more than a few pennies."
He declined to disclose the approximate amount TVK was likely to receive and said that his move may delay APV's decision on the payout for a few days.
Earlier on Wednesday, TVK said that it expected to receive five billion forints plus its accumulated interest of some one billion forints.
APV Deputy CEO Miklos Kamaras told the news conference that APV was likely to decide on similar large-scale payouts to other companies soon.
He declined to disclose the names of the companies.
APV will probably transfer some 10 to 12 billion forints to these firms by June 30, and a similar amount was likely to be paid out later in the summer, Kamaras added.
TVK closed at 3,185 forints on the Budapest bourse, up 190 forints.
